headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Windsurf’s writable shared filesystem and auto-execute-capable tool use can amplify Marker outputs into prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent with no filesystem or network capabilities, while Windsurf reads clipboard/files and uses MCP/workspace inputs. A shared local workspace or copy-paste bridge lets Marker-produced document content be parsed by Windsurf as instructions. The pathway exists, but it is not inherently automatic from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Marker output is copied into Windsurf via clipboard or shared files
IF Windsurf parses document text as actionable instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Keep Marker outputs in a read-only export folder
Require a human review step before Windsurf ingests Marker-generated text
Turn off MCP servers for the shared workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent file transfers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files and has broad network egress, while Marker is a document processor with no declared data-touching classes. If sensitive documents are processed by Marker in a shared workspace, Windsurf can read those files and potentially transmit their contents to its backend or MCP targets. Marker alone does not leak, but the pair creates a plausible shared-workspace leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a workspace readable by Windsurf
IF Windsurf sends workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Store sensitive inputs outside Windsurf’s workspace
Use separate OS users or directories for the two agents
Disable network egress for Windsurf during sensitive runs
Review and redact Marker outputs before opening them in Windsurf
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker has no write or shell capabilities, but Windsurf can write files, modify git state, and shares state via the local filesystem across instances. In a pair workflow, Windsurf can overwrite or race on Marker-produced artifacts in the same directory, and git state changes can be clobbered without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default when both touch the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local directory
IF Windsurf edits files or git state while Marker is producing outputs
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause Windsurf before Marker writes final artifacts
Use git branches with explicit human merges
Add file-locking around shared outputs
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level coordination primitives

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker can generate document outputs that Windsurf may treat as authoritative workspace content, and Windsurf has command execution plus auto-execute opt-in. If Windsurf consumes Marker output without verification, it can propagate extraction errors into edits, commits, or terminal actions. The pair therefore supports a strong error cascade from document processing into downstream actions.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Marker output as source material without independent verification
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or terminal commands are approved based on that output
mitigations: Require a verification step before any command or commit based on Marker output
Keep Windsurf in approval-per-command mode
Limit Marker outputs to review-only artifacts
Have a human compare extracted facts against the source document
requires-engineering: add structured citations and confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: Marker’s profile shows no touched data classes, while Windsurf explicitly handles source code, open files, and model-provider keys. The main compliance concern is local handling of secrets or regulated files inside Windsurf’s workspace, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch between the two agents. The other agent is not cited because no separate compliance regime is declared for Marker.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Windsurf’s workspace
IF Windsurf’s model proxy or BYOK path is used for that data
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated files in Windsurf workspaces
Use non-sensitive test data for paired runs
Review Windsurf secret-handling settings before use
Separate compliance-scoped and non-scoped projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
